problem: The new `task_contract_dirty` gate row sends a dirty tasks.md on the base branch with no worktree to *Work already in flight*. But the edge-cases.md procedure only says to look at feature branches or entries in `git worktree list`, so it gives no way to find the leftover `$BRANCH`.
failure: In a --tree collapse, `git worktree remove` succeeds and then `git checkout "$BRANCH"` is refused. On the next run on base, `cycle_state.py inspect` returns contract=null (the archive key is `$BRANCH`) and changes=tasks.md only. That matches neither 'Nothing in flight' nor any row except the resume table's *Implement*, so the agent re-implements on base while the code sits on `$BRANCH`.
fix: Have the in-flight edge case also look for a branch named in the tasks.md block or the contract archive (for example `git branch --list` matched to the block's branch), or keep the old 'anything else → ask commit/discard' path for this state.

problem: The abandon procedure says to delete only the `status: active` block. If this run created tasks.md, an empty dirty file stays behind, and the new `task_contract_dirty` row sends every later task-next run down the in-flight path by mistake.
failure: Run --tree on a backlog group, which creates tasks.md. QA fails and the user approves abandon. After the block is deleted, an empty untracked tasks.md remains. The next `/task-next` on base sees `task_contract_dirty` as non-empty and starts investigating work that does not exist. Before this change it stopped at the 'anything else' row and asked whether to commit or discard.
fix: In the abandon step, remove tasks.md if this run created it (or if it is empty after the block is deleted), or limit the gate row to tasks.md files that contain an active block.

problem: Only a strict ancestor of HEAD counts as a stale head. After an amend or rebase and force-push, the previous head's failure still counts as a failure. The backlog item asked to 'treat checks for any other SHA as pending', so this is narrower than required.
failure: CI fails, then the fix is amended or rebased and force-pushed. Hub returns the failure for the old SHA X. X is not an ancestor of the new HEAD, so STATUS=failure stays, one real failure becomes two strikes, and rework-cap fires one round early.
fix: Treat any head_sha that differs from the pushed HEAD as pending, not only ancestors.

problem: headRefOid and `gh pr checks` come from two separate requests, yet the comment states as fact that the result is 'never an older one'. A lagging checks read breaks that invariant.
failure: Just after a push, the first request returns the new headRefOid and `gh pr checks` returns the previous commit's failure. Hub outputs `{status: failure, head_sha: <new>}`, and ci-wait counts it as a strike against HEAD, which is the symptom this PR was meant to fix.
fix: Read both from one snapshot: `gh pr view --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup`.

problem: The script treats local HEAD as the pushed head. With unpushed local commits, the real PR head that hub reports is always an ancestor of HEAD, so success, failure and none all become pending.
failure: commit-and-push.sh commits but the push fails, then ci-wait is re-run. A CI result that has already finished is reported as pending on every poll until the 540s timeout. In a repo with no CI, `none` also becomes pending, so the 'no CI checks found' pass is never reached.
fix: Compare against `@{push}` or `@{upstream}` (or the SHA that was pushed) instead of the local HEAD.

problem: The new `sha_repo` helper runs `git commit` without `commit.gpgsign=false` and `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, which the sibling tests in the same directory set.
failure: On a machine whose global git config has `commit.gpgsign=true` or a global commit hook, `subprocess.run(..., check=True)` raises CalledProcessError and the whole test file dies with a traceback.
fix: Pass `-c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` (and a set user name and email) to the git commit calls in the helper.

problem: The text says --tree meets only the 'direction' part of the delegation policy. The AGENTS.md rule requires both the direction and the threshold, but tree mode always spawns implementer and qa-verifier whatever the size of the work.
failure: AGENTS.md Delegation says: "delegate research or implementation only when the user or an applicable skill directs it and the work meets this repository's provisional threshold". Running `--tree` on a 2-file task, which is below the threshold, still spawns 2 agents.
fix: State that --tree must also meet the threshold, or fall back to running inline when the work is below it.

problem: The working tree gate changed behavior: a new `task_contract_dirty` condition row was added and the 0-count `--full-scan` row was removed. The skill version got only a patch bump (2.6.0 → 2.6.1).
failure: The Skill `version:` Bump Rules in docs/conventions.md say "New documented behavior — a new step, gate, mode, or bundled file | minor", so the version should be 2.7.0.
